newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's foreign debt falls to $31 bln at end 95/96.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's foreign debt falls to $31 bln at end 95/96.

text.p: Egypt's foreign debt fell to $31.043 billion at the end of the financial year 1995/96 from $32.965 billion one year earlier, said a central bank report made available on Tuesday. The years end on June 30.
Cairo's foreign currency reserves are ample at $18.5 billion so it does not need to resort to new foreign borrowing.
On Friday the International Monetary Fund board approved an economic reform agreement with Egypt, paving the way for the Paris Club to write off a further $4 billion in debt.
The $4 billion is the last tranche of the $10 billion in official debt the Paris Club agreed to waive under an agreement reached with Egypt after the Gulf War in 1991.
The waiver will take the external debt below $28 billion.
